quotes.text: A loss scarcely remains a loss for an hour: in some way or other a gift from heaven has always fallen into our lap at the same moment, a new form of strength, for example: be it but a new opportunity for the exercise of strength!
quotes.plain: Every loss hands you something, even if it's just a chance to get stronger.

quotes.text: One is now ashamed of repose: even long reflection almost causes remorse of conscience.
quotes.plain: We've come to feel guilty for resting or thinking slowly. That's a sickness.

quotes.text: Thinking is done with a stop-watch, as dining is done with the eyes fixed on the financial newspaper; we live like men who are continually "afraid of letting opportunities slip."
quotes.plain: Rushing after every opportunity makes you worse at thinking and at living.

quotes.text: Work is winning over more and more the good conscience to its side: the desire for enjoyment already calls itself "need of recreation," and even begins to be ashamed of itself.
quotes.plain: Work has gotten so holy that even pleasure has to apologize and call itself recovery.

quotes.text: The thinker does not need applause nor the clapping of hands, provided he be sure of the clapping of his own hands: the latter, however, he cannot do without.
quotes.plain: You can live without the crowd's praise. You can't live without your own.

quotes.text: There has perhaps been an evil hour for every philosopher, in which he thought: What do I matter, if people should not believe my poor arguments!
quotes.plain: Every serious person has a night where they ask if any of it matters. Expect it.

quotes.text: He also who loves himself must have learned it in this way: there is no other way. Love also has to be learned.
quotes.plain: Even loving yourself is a skill you build over time, not a feeling you wait for.

quotes.text: How many men are there who know how to observe? And among the few who do know, how many observe themselves?
quotes.plain: Almost nobody watches themselves honestly. Start there.

quotes.text: We, however, would seek to become what we are, the new, the unique, the incomparable, making laws for ourselves and creating ourselves!
quotes.plain: Don't copy anyone. Become the specific person you are and write your own rules.

quotes.text: Ah, how little you know of the happiness of man, you comfortable and good-natured ones! for happiness and misfortune are brother and sister, and twins, who grow tall together, or, as with you, remain small together!
quotes.plain: Joy and hardship grow together. Dodge one and you stay small at both.

quotes.text: Put at least the skin of three centuries betwixt thyself and the present day! And the clamour of the present day, the noise of wars and revolutions, ought to be a murmur to thee!
quotes.plain: Step back from today's noise until it's a murmur and you can hear yourself.

quotes.text: At last the horizon seems open once more, granting even that it is not bright; our ships can at last put out to sea in face of every danger; every hazard is again permitted to the discerner; the sea, our sea, again lies open before us; perhaps never before did such an "open sea" exist.
quotes.plain: When the old map breaks, the sea is open. Dark, but yours to sail.

quotes.text: "Selflessness" has no value either in heaven or on earth; the great problems all demand great love, and it is only the strong, well-rounded, secure spirits, those who have a solid basis, that are qualified for them.
quotes.plain: Erasing yourself helps no one. Big problems need a strong, whole person.

quotes.text: So much distrust, so much philosophy!
quotes.plain: Doubt is where thinking starts.

quotes.text: How much faith a person requires in order to flourish, how much "fixed opinion" he requires which he does not wish to have shaken, because he holds himself thereby, is a measure of his power (or more plainly speaking, of his weakness).
quotes.plain: The more certainty you need to stay upright, the weaker you are.

quotes.text: Belief is always most desired, most pressingly needed where there is a lack of will: for the will, as emotion of command, is the distinguishing characteristic of sovereignty and power.
quotes.plain: People grab for something to obey when they can't command themselves.

quotes.text: Is it not possible that it should be the instinct of fear which enjoins upon us to know?
quotes.plain: Maybe our hunger for answers is really just fear wanting to feel safe.

quotes.text: The known is the accustomed, and the accustomed is the most difficult of all to "understand," that is to say, to perceive as a problem, to perceive as strange, distant, "outside of us."
quotes.plain: What's familiar is the hardest to see clearly. You stop questioning what you're used to.

quotes.text: We do not belong to those who only get their thoughts from books, or at the prompting of books, it is our custom to think in the open air, walking, leaping, climbing, or dancing on lonesome mountains by preference, or close to the sea, where even the paths become thoughtful.
quotes.plain: Think on your feet outside, not just from books at a desk.

quotes.text: Every kind of perfection is purchased at a high price on earth, where everything is perhaps purchased too dear; one is an expert in one's department at the price of being also a victim of one's department.
quotes.plain: Mastery has a price. Getting great at one thing bends the rest of you.

quotes.text: We grow like trees, that is difficult to understand, like all life! not in one place, but everywhere, not in one direction only, but upwards and outwards, as well as inwards and downwards.
quotes.plain: Growth isn't one clean line. You grow in every direction at once, including down.

quotes.text: But we do as we have always done: we take whatever is cast into us down into our depths, for we are deep, we do not forget, and once more grow clear....
quotes.plain: Take what people throw at you, let it sink, and come back clear.

quotes.text: There are hours in which I am ashamed of it; to be sure there are likewise hours in which I am ashamed of this shame.
quotes.plain: Feeling ashamed of what you don't know, then ashamed of the shame. Everyone loops like that.

quotes.text: Not fat, but the greatest suppleness and power is what a good dancer wishes from his nourishment, and I know not what the spirit of a philosopher would like better than to be a good dancer.
quotes.plain: Want to be light and strong, not heavy and comfortable.
